title: Manifesto of the Communist Party
author: Karl Marx and Frederick Engels
translator: Samuel Moore (1888) in cooperation with Frederick Engels
version: Marxists Internet Archive (marxists.org) 2005 PDF edition; from Marx/Engels Selected Works, Vol 1, Progress Publishers, 1969
page_counting_rule: Excluded page 1 (title & publication information page). Counted pages 2–44 as valid content pages (43 content pages >= 30 required by rubric).

chapters.title: Introduction / Preamble
chapters.description: Opening statement: 'A spectre is haunting Europe — the spectre of communism' and purpose of the Manifesto.

chapters.title: Bourgeois and Proletarians
chapters.description: Historical development of class struggle, rise of modern bourgeoisie, globalization of commerce, and emergence of proletariat.

chapters.title: Proletarians and Communists
chapters.description: Relationship between Communists and the working class, abolition of private property, family, nationality, and the 10-point programme.

chapters.title: Socialist and Communist Literature
chapters.description: Critique of contemporary socialist schools: Reactionary, Conservative/Bourgeois, and Critical-Utopian.

chapters.title: Position of the Communists in Relation to the Various Existing Opposition Parties
chapters.description: Tactics and alliances of Communists across European countries (France, Switzerland, Poland, Germany) and the concluding battle cry.

chapters.title: Prefaces to Various Language Editions
chapters.description: Historical prefaces written by Marx and Engels describing translations, revolutions, and the international spread of the Manifesto.

metadata_fields_for_filter.rationale: Filters queries by core conceptual section (e.g. theoretical class struggle in Chapter I vs concrete political program in Chapter II vs prefaces in Appendix).

metadata_fields_for_filter.source: Sub-headings inside Chapter III and Appendix
metadata_fields_for_filter.rationale: Allows fine-grained filtering by specific sub-sections, editions, or critique types.
